title: Production Readiness Sprintboard and Uncertainty Ledger
content:
Purpose:
Capture sprint-level delivery tasks tied to explicit KPI targets and surface uncertainties with clear mitigations. This sheet is both a sprintboard (work -> owners -> dates) and an "uncertainty ledger" (risks framed as confidence gaps with ownerable mitigations). Use during launch prep and the final go/no-go review.

Quick summary: This artifact is designed to be a compact operational control plane for Product Ops + Eng + SRE + Sales Ops during feature launches. It ties three things together: 1) What we will deliver next two sprints, 2) Which KPIs those deliveries are expected to move, and 3) The open uncertainties (confidence < 85%) that could materially affect launch.

How to use (running cadence):
- Update sprintboard rows at the start of each planning session.
- Update confidence numbers in the ledger after spike/experiment results or when blocking issues change.
- Product Ops owns the weekly readiness digest to execs; engineering owners own task status and mitigation updates.

Sprintboard columns (explainers):
- ID: short alphanumeric (SB-###)
- Task title: concise action (feature flag, canary config, infra resize)
- Owner: one person accountable (name)
- Lead team: e.g., eng-serving-runtime, eng-sre, product-hosted-api
- Sprint window: sprint# or date range (e.g., S31 2026-01-12 -> 2026-01-26)
- Status: todo | in_progress | blocked | done
- Dependencies: Jira keys or brief notes (external teams)
- KPI tie: short name of KPI(s) expected to move (see KPI tracker section)
- Acceptance criteria: pass/fail criteria for marking done

Sprintboard (example rows - update live):
SB-001, "Canary rollout for host-api v2", Arjun Patel, eng-serving-runtime, S32 2026-01-26 -> 2026-02-09, in_progress, JIRA-2183; monitoring config pending, KPI tie: mean_p95_latency_ms; Acceptance: <150ms p95 on canary for 24h and no error spike >0.5%
SB-002, "KV cache warmup + preload hook", Priya Kapoor, eng-platform, S32, todo, none, KPI tie: token_cost_per_1k, Acceptance: KV hit-rate >70% in test workload
SB-003, "Fallback model variant & routing policy", Leo García, product-ops, S32, blocked, model-team signoff, KPI tie: availability_slo, Acceptance: automated fallback triggered in sim and served within 200ms

Uncertainty Ledger (CSV-like lines):
UL-ID,Description,Owner,Confidence_pct,Mitigation_Action,Action_Owner,Impact,Primary_KPI,Readiness_Gate
UL-101,"Quantization regression vs finetuned prompt sets", Maya Chen,72,"add graded eval harness + revert profile","Ethan Nguyen (mlops)",High,output_quality_score,gate-B
UL-102,"Autoscaling slow to recover on sudden bursts", Arjun Patel,60,"stress test with 3x traffic spike; pre-warmed buffer","SRE Team (lead: Jenna)",High,availability_slo,gate-A
UL-103,"Embedding index memory blowout for long-running tenant queries", Priya Kapoor,80,"TTL-based eviction + soft-eviction config","Infra (lead: Luis)",Medium,median_query_cost,gate-B
UL-104,"Client SDK wide rollout compatibility (older clients)", Leo García,88,"compat shim + opt-in deprecation header","Developer Experience (lead: Sam)",Low,adoption_rate,gate-C

Confidence guidance: confidence_pct is a subjective composite of experimental evidence (50%), prod-sim results (30%), and owner judgement (20%). Use whole numbers. Anything under 85% should have an explicit mitigation and an owner.

KPI Tracker (compact):
Each KPI row: KPI_ID | KPI name | baseline | launch_target | measurement_window | alert_threshold | notes
KP-01 | mean_p95_latency_ms | 210ms | <=150ms | 1h rolling | >=170ms (warning) | measured at edge LB
KP-02 | token_cost_per_1k | $2.40 | <=$1.80 | daily | >$2.10 (warning) | depends on batching configs
KP-03 | availability_slo | 99.90% | >=99.95% | 24h | <99.92% (warning) | includes fallbacks
KP-04 | output_quality_score | 0.87 | >=0.90 | weekly | drop >0.02 | evaluated via seeded eval prompts

Readiness Gates (three-tier recommended):
- Gate A (Must pass): Core infra + availability, emergency fallback in place, primary KPI guardrails green. Signoff: SRE lead + Eng lead.
- Gate B (High confidence): Quality regression tolerance, canary validation complete against critical prompt sets. Signoff: Product + Applied ML lead.
- Gate C (Optional, recommended): Feature completeness, secondary metrics (cost/latency) at target, enablement docs and sales playbook ready. Signoff: Product Ops + GTM lead.

Acceptance rubric (example):
- Green = all Gate A + at least one of Gate B/C satisfied (proceed)
- Yellow = Gate A satisfied, outstanding Gate B mitigations that have timeboxed plans (consider delayed or limited rollout)
- Red = Gate A failed (hold launch)

Go/No-Go checklist (to read during decision call):
1) Are all Gate A acceptance criteria met for the last 24h? (SRE + Eng lead verify)
2) Are any UL items >75% impact and confidence <60% unresolved? If yes, escalate or freeze that surface area.
3) Are KPIs within warning thresholds? If any critical KPI is in red, require mitigation demonstration or automatic fallback tested.
4) Do we have rollback + emergency contact plan documented? (Ops runbook link in linked_artifacts)
5) GTM brief: do customer-facing docs match the product behavior? (Product Ops signoff)

Operational notes / conventions:
- Tagging: Use the UL-ID when creating Jira issues to link mitigation work to the ledger (e.g., JIRA-2147 -> UL-101).
- Communication: Weekly digest posted to #launch-readiness with current color and top 3 UL items.
- Ownership: If an owner changes, explicitly edit the UL row and add an update comment with date.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight (one sheet) to be copy-pasted into launch playbooks or exported as CSV for stakeholder briefings.
- Feedback requested: additional KPI definitions to include (especially business-facing adoption metrics) and whether we should lower the confidence threshold to 80% for certain low-impact features.

History / recent changes:
- 2025-11-08: initial skeleton created (Maya)
- 2025-12-02: added KPI rows and Gate definitions (Priya)
- 2026-01-14: added UL-102 after observed autoscaler behavior in stress test (Arjun)
- 2026-02-10: updated acceptance criteria for canary latency (Maya)

End of sheet. Keep this document as the single source of truth for sprint-level launch readiness for the current release window.
